sentences.text:
Parchuri Suresh vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 16
September, 2019

entities.text: Parchuri Suresh vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5154 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioners/A1 to A4, A6, A9, A13 to A16 and A18 to 30 seek to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.59 of 2019 on the file of Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Giddalur, which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 273, 188 and 353 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').

entities.text: Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Giddalur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 04.01.2017 at 18.00 hours, when the complainant along with his staff proceeded to Rentachintala Gate Centre in Giddalur Town at sanjeevareddy Nagar, on suspicion, caught the accused and found the banned tobacco products in their possession and hence, arrested them and seized the same and registered a case in Crime No.234 of 2017 of Giddalur Police Station, for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.

As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.
4.

So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto basing on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police of Giddalur Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners/accused under Sections 273 and 188 of IPC and Sections 58, 59 and 63 of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
